4. READ IT HERE FIRST

 

Timber was gold in the South—until a market collapse crushed the forest economy.

 

Pulpwood helped launch the South’s industrial era. Mill closures have axed demand, marking the biggest threat since the fall of King Cotton. The South, and Georgia in particular, has borne the brunt of a historic run of pulp and paper-mill closures as recycled boxes, cheap imported pulp and more thrifty packing by e-commerce giants, including Amazon.com, have hit demand. 5.

 

The Warren Buffett of the NFL is on a quest to win in a league built for losers.

 

No sport punishes winning as ruthlessly as pro football. But Los Angeles Rams GM Les Snead found a way to build a perennial contender by making bold bets and hunting for value where others weren’t looking. After the 2020 season, Snead had an epiphany: To win a championship, everything that had carried the Rams to that point would have to change. That realization triggered the most aggressive set of all-in moves ever attempted by an NFL franchise, as Snead traded away his starting quarterback and draft picks for proven veterans ready to win.
